simple.meaning: בִּאוּשׁ (biʼûwsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “wicked.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Ezra, beginning at Ezra 4:12. Its contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בִּאוּשׁ (H873).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H873. bish [ בִּאישׁ K § 11, 8b )] adjective bad (so Egyptian Aramaic Cooke 75. 2 ; בִּישׁ ᵑ7 , Syriac ); — feminine singular emphatic וּבִאישְׁתָּא Ezra 4:12 rebellious and bad city (not בִּאוּשְׁתָָּא , see Baer n .). בָּתַר בָּאתַר, see אֲתַר .
